title: 2 Chronicles 31
paragraphs: ¹ When all this was finished, every Israelite who had come to Jerusalem went out to the towns of Judah and smashed the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and demolished the high places and altars all across Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh, until they had utterly destroyed them all. Then every Israelite returned to his own land and city. ² Hezekiah organized the priests and Levites in their groups, assigning each man to his particular duty — whether for burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, for service, for giving thanks, or for praise at the gates of the LORD's camp. ³ From his own resources, the king designated a portion for the morning and evening burnt offerings, the sabbath burnt offerings, the New Moon offerings, and all the appointed feasts, as prescribed in the law of the LORD. ⁴ He also commanded the people of Jerusalem to give the priests and Levites their proper portion, so that they could devote themselves fully to the law of the LORD. ⁵ As soon as the order went out, the Israelites responded generously with the firstfruits of grain, new wine, olive oil, and honey — indeed, the firstfruits of all their crops — and they brought in a large tithe of everything.

⁶ The Israelites and people of Judah who lived in the towns of Judah also brought in the tithe of their cattle and sheep, and the tithe of the things consecrated to the LORD their God, piling them up in great heaps. ⁷ They began piling up the heaps in the third month and finished in the seventh. ⁸ When Hezekiah and his officials came and saw the heaps, they praised the LORD and his people Israel. ⁹ Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the heaps. ¹⁰ Azariah the chief priest, from the house of Zadok, replied, "Since the people began bringing their contributions to the house of the LORD, we have had more than enough to eat and a large amount left over — the LORD has blessed his people, and this great supply is what remains."

¹¹ Then Hezekiah ordered storerooms to be prepared in the house of the LORD, and this was done. ¹² The offerings, tithes, and consecrated items were faithfully brought in. Cononiah the Levite was in charge of these, and his brother Shimei was second in command. ¹³ Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah served as supervisors under Cononiah and Shimei, by the appointment of King Hezekiah and Azariah, the chief official of the house of God. ¹⁴ Kore son of Imnah, a Levite who was keeper of the East Gate, was in charge of the freewill offerings given to God, distributing the contributions for the LORD and the most holy gifts. ¹⁵ Under him, Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah faithfully assisted him in distributing portions to the priests in their cities — both great and small alike — according to their divisions.

¹⁶ In addition to the males registered by genealogy from three years old and upward, provision was made for everyone who entered the house of the LORD to receive their daily portion for their service according to their assigned duties and divisions. ¹⁷ The registration of the priests was by their family lineage, and the Levites twenty years old and upward were listed by their duties and divisions. ¹⁸ The genealogical record also covered all the priests' and Levites' little children, their wives, their sons, and their daughters — the whole congregation — since they had consecrated themselves faithfully in the holy work. ¹⁹ As for the sons of Aaron, the priests living in the pasture lands around their cities, in every city there were men designated by name to distribute portions to every male among the priests and to all registered Levites. ²⁰ This is how Hezekiah handled things throughout all of Judah — doing what was good, right, and faithful before the LORD his God.
²¹ In everything he undertook — whether in the service of the house of God, in obeying the law, or in keeping the commandments — he sought his God with his whole heart. And he prospered.
